A1.justification: Both complete 25-page PDFs describe the same TokenSwift work and include Appendices A-H. Pages 2-25 have identical extracted text and rendered content; the scientific content on page 1 also matches.

before.justification: v1 reports original PG-19 generation experiments, including speedup and acceptance-rate results in Tables 3-4, component ablations, repetition analyses and appendix training-loss curves.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results, including Tables 3-4, the main-text and appendix ablations, generation examples and training-loss curves.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Algorithm 1 are identical, retaining multi-token self-drafting, token reutilization, dynamic KV-cache management, contextual penalty and the same verification procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use PG-19 for training and ultra-long generation evaluation. Appendix C retains Wikipedia and C4-en for draft-model training. No datasets, tasks or test scenarios are added or removed.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains TriForce and both MagicDec draft configurations. Table 3 retains Medusa* and TriForce*, with AR as the speedup reference. Comparator membership and adaptations are unchanged.

E3.justification: The model configurations, data splits, prefill and generation lengths, sampling settings, training budgets and evaluation procedures remain identical. Acceptance rate, speedup and Distinct-n metrics are unchanged.

E4.justification: Sections 4.3-4.4 and Appendices D, F-H retain the same component ablations, tree and sampling analyses, temperature/prefill/penalty sensitivity studies, repetition cases and training-loss curves.

E5.justification: Section 4.2 retains the statement that results are averaged over five experiments with standard deviations. Tables 3-4 retain identical uncertainty reporting, with no added seed information or statistical procedures.

E6.justification: Numerical results, plotted findings and generation examples are identical throughout both PDFs. For example, Table 3 retains the 3.27 ± 0.19 speedup for LLaMA3.1-8b with 4,096-token prefill and 100K-token output.

T1.justification: Equations 1-6, Appendix A's speculative-decoding losslessness derivation, and the sampling and tree-attention formulations in Appendices D-E are unchanged. No definitions, assumptions or proofs are revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims of lossless acceleration up to 100K tokens, over threefold speedup across model scales and architectures, and mitigation of repetitive generation.

C2.justification: Both versions give identical explanations of speedup mechanisms, verification-cost and diversity tradeoffs, and repetition limitations. Applicability qualifications and interpretations in the appendices are also unchanged.

D1.justification: Section 4.1 and Appendices B-C retain identical hardware, hyperparameters, inference settings and draft-model training details. Code and data access information, including their link targets, is unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 5, the bibliography and in-text citations are identical. The positioning relative to speculative decoding and long-sequence generation research remains unchanged.

P1.justification: The first-page date and arXiv version/date stamp are updated. The embedded PDF title metadata changes to 'TokenSwift: Lossless Acceleration of Ultra Long Sequence Generation', but the printed title, prose and section structure remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 1-7, Tables 1-16, the decoding-tree diagram, captions and page arrangements are unchanged. The first-page date/version text updates do not change the layout or scientific displays.

improvement.justification: The scientific exposition, methods, empirical evidence, theoretical material and reproducibility details are identical, including all appendices. The limited date/version and PDF metadata updates provide no meaningful improvement or deterioration in overall paper quality.
